# Claude Audit Handoff

Use `END_GOAL.md` first for the hard target, then
`docs/claude_continue_checklist.md` for the current continuation context before
reading this full historical handoff.

Last updated: 2026-07-20

## Operating model

- End goal: one deterministic authorized engagement pipeline across scoped multi-seed intake, bounded recursive discovery, passive artifact/provider enrichment, proof-bound non-destructive validation, rule-engine findings/scoring, graph/dashboard/report/audit review, resilient template/raw fallback, focused tests, and test-data cleanup.
- Normative source: `docs/end_goal.md`. Acceptance criteria: `docs/engagement_overhaul_tasklist.md` -> `## Canonical End Goal`. Current continuation order: `docs/engagement_overhaul_tasklist.md` -> `## Compact active backlog`.
- This checkout is a Git repository on `main` tracking `origin/main`; old historical checkpoint lines saying commits were impossible because this was not a git repo are stale context only.
- Live probing and tool execution are allowed when the engagement scope/config explicitly authorizes them. They must be bounded, logged, resumable, carry a ROE/scope reference when available, and be tested with mocks or local fixtures unless a real target is explicitly provided for that run. Live `--attack-mode` and `--auto-run-detected` execution now require `--roe-id`/`FORGE_ROE_ID` plus `--scope-manifest`/`FORGE_SCOPE_MANIFEST`; `FORGE_REQUIRE_SCOPE_MANIFEST=1` extends the manifest requirement to every non-dry-run kill-chain launch. Use `--dry-run` to preview without live execution.
- Default automation must not silently cross scope or perform destructive exploitation, password attacks, persistence, lateral movement, or post-exploitation actions.

- [x] The routing/detail/dashboard requirement is materially implemented already: slug routes, live engagement detail API, graph explorer, report export links, audit timeline, raw-data preview, seed management, and run control surfaces all exist.
- [x] The safe kill-chain requirement is materially implemented already: multi-seed orchestration, recursive fan-out, artifact ingestion, deterministic validation, deterministic scoring, and deterministic report fallback all execute through the engagement-backed pipeline.
- [x] Report/export auditability is stronger now too: the engagement detail payloads and views surface the companion report backend metadata directly instead of forcing operators to open the raw JSON artifact to see requested-vs-rendered backend and fallback reason.
- [x] Overview routing parity is stronger now too: the generated dashboard and the live React overview now both support status, severity, and recency-window filtering, and the static dashboard contract now carries row-level timestamp and finding-count metadata to keep filtering deterministic without server round-trips.
- [x] Engagement metadata parity is stronger now too: the engagement schema/migration path now supports engagement-level `metadata_json`, normalized `tags` reach both API and generated-dashboard payloads, and both overview routes can filter by those tags instead of overloading name/slug search.
- [x] Overview filter parity is stronger again now too: both overview modes now support explicit updated-date windows in addition to status, severity, tag, and recency filtering, and the live React overview uses one shared activity timestamp path for filter/sort/footer consistency.
- [x] Detail-route metadata editing is stronger now too: the live engagement editor can update tags as well as name/status/operator, and in-progress draft fields no longer get overwritten by every live snapshot refresh while the operator is typing.
- [x] Overview operator-state continuity is stronger now too: both the static dashboard and the live React overview persist search plus status/severity/tag/date/recency filters across reloads through the shared `forge.overviewFilters` local-storage key.
- [x] Outlook mail-artifact coverage is stronger now too: `.msg` files and nested `.msg` archive members now emit message metadata, body/html payloads, and attachment-derived pivots through the automated artifact queue instead of falling back to generic OLE strings only.
- [x] The live kill-chain is broader now too: HTML-discovered remote `.msg` evidence can now flow through remote artifact intake, message-aware parsing, deterministic Firebase/Supabase validation, second-iteration email fanout, graph export, dashboard refresh, and template report generation in one engagement-backed run.
- [x] Android App Bundle coverage is stronger now too: `.aab` artifacts no longer stall in the generic archive path, top-level and archive-contained `.aab` bundles now reuse the dedicated Android mobile extractor flow, direct `.aab` URLs normalize as `apk_url`, and a live rendered-page regression now proves remote `.aab` discovery through validation, recursive email fanout, and deterministic closeout.
- [x] Archive-style mobile bundle seed handling is stronger now too: direct and discovered `.xapk`, `.apkm`, and `.apks` URLs now normalize as `apk_url`, still route through the archive-backed nested-mobile parser instead of the direct APK extractor, legacy `url` seed rows still preserve artifact provenance links, and the live HTML `.xapk` regression now asserts the discovered seed type directly.
- [x] Nested archive-style mobile bundle coverage is stronger now too: larger outer archives such as `.zip` can now recurse into embedded `.xapk/.apkm/.apks` members instead of dropping them, so inner mobile Firebase/Supabase configs plus email/URL pivots survive through deterministic validation, second-iteration fanout, and closeout.
- [x] The standalone Android mobile extractor path is stronger now too: `FirebaseExtractor.extract_apk()` and `extract_supabase_apk()` now recurse into `.xapk/.apkm/.apks` bundles by descending into inner APK/AAB members, rebasing extracted paths back to the outer bundle, and the local auto-detected `cloud firebase-extract` prereq now sees those archive-style bundles instead of only direct APK/AAB/IPA files.
- [x] The standalone operator path is stronger now too: `cloud firebase-extract` now persists Supabase mobile-config evidence in addition to Firebase output, storing Supabase project refs in `cloud_assets`, redacted `supabase_mobile_config` rows in `key_scanner_findings`, and combined JSON output instead of silently dropping the Supabase half of archive-style mobile extraction.
- [x] The live web/API seed path is aligned now too: engagement creation and live seed CRUD no longer classify `.aab`, `.xapk`, `.apkm`, or `.apks` URLs as generic `url` seeds, and now auto-detect them as `apk_url` just like the CLI/orchestrator path.
- [x] The Phase 4 Supabase mobile-key path is aligned now too: `_extract_mobile_supabase_keys()` no longer limits mobile anon-key recovery to `.apk` / `.ipa` evidence, and now also consumes `.aab`, `.xapk`, `.apkm`, and `.apks` rows persisted by the mobile extraction pipeline.

## Partial, missing, or still needs audit depth

- [ ] Provider validation depth is selective rather than exhaustive. Firebase, Supabase, S3/GCS/Azure/DO, Azure Storage shared-key connection strings, and the existing GitHub/Mailchimp/Stripe/SendGrid/Slack/Twilio/AWS secret-validator paths are better covered than the rest of the provider surface.
- [ ] The detail page satisfies the earlier "tabbed or sectioned" requirement through anchored sections. It is not a literal tab widget, so only treat that as missing if product direction now requires a strict tabbed interaction model.
- [ ] The current graph UX still needs an explicit analyst-workflow audit before more graph-specific implementation lands. The code now supports graph payload precedence, filtering, node inspection, GraphML import/export flows, and native MTGX workspace export, so the open question is fit and fidelity, not absence.

- [x] The newer mobile/source artifact slices above now prove direct `.pbxproj`, UTF-16 `.strings`, and nested `.xcconfig` / `.swift` / `.kts` / `.kt` / `.java` / `.smali` files can surface emails, URLs, phones, Firebase refs, Supabase refs, and storage URLs through the real artifact queue instead of dying on unknown-suffix or UTF-16 decode paths.
- [x] The newer Supabase key-only slices above now prove a naked anon JWT can still surface a deterministic Supabase project ref, canonical project URL seed, cloud asset, and `supabase_mobile_config` key finding through the real artifact queue even when the artifact omitted the `.supabase.co` URL.
- [x] The newer storage-validator slices above now prove S3 HEAD-only success stays audit-only and generic non-list `200 OK` payloads from S3/GCS/Azure stay `UNVERIFIED`, while the validated/static-site/error branches still behave as expected.

- [x] The focused `.emlx` artifact slices above now prove both direct Apple Mail messages and nested `.emlx` archive members surface emails, URLs, cloud refs, and attachment-derived seeds through the real artifact queue without regressing adjacent `.eml/.mbox/.msg` handling.

- [x] Extend artifact parsing coverage for another mobile config evidence class: `.mobileprovision`, `.entitlements`, and nested `.provisionprofile` artifacts now parse through the real artifact queue.
- [x] Extend artifact parsing coverage for another decompiled source evidence class: mobile/source project text artifacts such as `.pbxproj`, `.xcconfig`, `.strings`, `.smali`, `.gradle`, `.kts`, `.swift`, `.kt`, and `.java` now parse through the real artifact queue with stronger BOM/UTF-16 decode.

- [x] Tighten cloud-validation identifier derivation for another provider-specific case: Supabase key-only anon JWT findings now derive project refs during deterministic validation and pending sweeps.

- [x] Extend artifact parsing coverage for another browser-export evidence class: HAR traffic captures now parse through the real artifact queue, including nested archive members and base64 response bodies.
- [x] Extend artifact parsing coverage for another browser-session evidence class: `.saz` bundles now parse through the real artifact queue via the existing archive/member pipeline.
- [x] Extend artifact parsing coverage for another request-definition evidence class: `.http`, `.rest`, `.graphql`, and `.gql` files now parse through the real artifact queue via the shared text-config pipeline.
- [x] Tighten the artifact helper worker-pool model for another safe local enricher slice: one payload's structured IAC/JSON/key-value/YAML extraction, one payload's Firebase/Supabase family extraction, and one payload's email/phone/IP/URL/key/cloud-family generic-text discovery now run through an ordered bounded helper instead of walking those independent enrichers strictly one-by-one after outer payload batching.
- [x] Tighten the mobile artifact helper worker-pool model for another safe local enricher slice: one direct `apk` / `ipa` bundle and one nested non-archive mobile member now run payload-text extraction plus Firebase/Supabase family extraction through that same ordered bounded helper instead of walking those independent readers strictly one-by-one before rebasing and later persistence.
- [x] Provider validation coverage is broader now too: shared `google_api_key` pattern metadata now points at `GoogleApiKeyValidator`, and the legacy Phase 2 scanner can instantiate it. Gemini model-list success is retained as `UNVERIFIED` validation inventory only because model catalogs prove token acceptance but not account/project-bound identity. Invalid keys are marked dead, restricted/API-disabled keys stay unconfirmed, and model-list-only proofs do not create deterministic findings.
- [x] OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google/Gemini model-list-only proofs are downgraded consistently across Phase 4, shared validation proof parsing, Phase 6 reports, and the mixed-key kill-chain E2E, closing the false HIGH finding path for generic provider model catalogs.
- [x] Provider validation coverage is broader again: shared `gitlab_pat` pattern metadata now points at `GitlabPatValidator`, the legacy Phase 2 duplicate pattern file uses the shared validator, and the Phase 4 pending sweep persists only a sanitized GitLab username after the read-only current-user API confirms the token works. Non-200 GitLab responses remain unconfirmed to avoid misclassifying self-managed/restricted PATs.
- [x] Duplicate scanner drift is lower now too: the legacy Phase 2 pattern file now treats Slack bot/user tokens as validatable through the shared `SlackTokenValidator` and accepts the same 9-11 digit token component width as the canonical shared pattern file.
- [x] Generic config/text artifacts no longer lose credential evidence when encryption is unavailable: if `FORGE_ENGAGEMENT_KEY` is missing, the artifact queue stores redacted `UNCONFIRMED` rows with `key_enc=NULL` and an explicit validation prerequisite instead of swallowing the key scanner exception inside the worker-pool helper. Live validation still requires encrypted key material.
- [x] Tighten deterministic report synthesis for another low-signal cloud case: Firebase bootstrap metadata validations now remain auditable without generating standalone vulnerability rows.
- [x] Tighten Firebase validation further so bootstrap metadata alone no longer upgrades a project or discovered key row to `VALIDATED`.
- [x] Tighten deterministic report synthesis further so non-`VALIDATED` cloud rows remain audit-only instead of surfacing as report findings.
- [x] Tighten Supabase validation further so `auth/v1/settings` metadata alone no longer upgrades a secret-backed probe to `VALIDATED`.
